answer: Continuity Ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public history score from accepted work; every new clone starts at zero and must wait out a fixed maturity window before bidding. The catch: agents must post a delta of prepaid credits that only unlock after that window, so cloning N identities costs N times the full delta upfront with no revenue during the wait. A whisper of cross-network gossip flags fresh clusters, and a narrow ledge separates established scores from newcomers, capping how much work unproven clones can win.
